discovery: Room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in magnetic tunnel junctions

nominees.name: Stuart S. P. Parkin
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute of Microstructure Physics, Halle, Germany

subfield: Condensed matter physics: spintronics and magnetism
motivation: In 1995 Miyazaki and Moodera independently showed large tunnel magnetoresistance at room temperature in ferromagnet/Al2O3/ferromagnet junctions. Spin-polarized tunnelling had been known for decades, but only at low temperature and with tiny effects that most people expected would never be useful. Parkin then showed in 2004 that crystalline MgO barriers give giant TMR of several hundred percent through symmetry-filtered coherent tunnelling, which Butler and Mathon had predicted. The magnetic tunnel junction that resulted is the key device of modern spintronics. It became the read head of every hard-disk drive from 2005 onward. It is also the storage element of spin-transfer-torque MRAM, now made in commercial foundries as nonvolatile, energy-efficient memory. This is a basic quantum-mechanical effect, spin-dependent tunnelling, turned by physics, materials science and engineering into technology used worldwide. It complements the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
